# Read-back

A weeknight stir-fry dinner for two people is being prepared in approximately 35 minutes by one cook working with two burners. The dish consists of jasmine rice that must cook first (the longest component, requiring rinsing, boiling, simmering and steaming), while chicken thighs are prepped and marinated and broccoli, garlic and ginger are chopped and a sauce is mixed. The stir-fry itself is quick—the wok is heated until smoking, chicken is seared and set aside, broccoli is steamed with a lid, garlic and ginger are added, then chicken and sauce are returned and tossed together. The rice must be off heat and steaming when the wok heating begins so everything finishes together hot and ready to plate. There is no explicit finish deadline; the goal is to complete the meal as soon as the work allows. The constraints are one cook, two burners (one for the rice pot, one for the wok), and the timing requirement that the rice steaming and the stir-fry cooking overlap so both are ready to serve at the same moment.
